clue.text: Metal washing machine?

blocks.note: first meaning: the reddish metallic element
second meaning: an old-fashioned large boiler in which laundry was heated and washed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'washing machine' is the old household boiler, a big metal tub of the same name, rather than a modern appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the chemical element Cu and the large tub once used on wash day to boil clothes.

clue.text: Sign to appeal to males

blocks.note: O is the exclamation of appeal, as in 'O come all ye faithful'
males are men

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a placard meant to attract the attention of men.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a token or indication of something to come.

clue.text: One way to shoulder the job of team selection

blocks.note: first meaning: carrying someone on your back, with their arms round your shoulders
second meaning: read as three words, choosing a player for one of the defensive positions in football or rugby

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word into PICK A BACK: a back is a defensive player, so choosing one is part of selecting a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Piggyback carrying, rider on the bearer's back holding the shoulders, is one way of taking a load onto them.

clue.text: I creep around helping in the kitchen

indicators.note: creeping around suggests moving about aimlessly, so the letters of the preceding words wander out of order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A kitchen helper tiptoes about quietly while lending a hand with the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cooking instructions is a cook's aid, something that assists whoever prepares food.

clue.text: Didn't stay uninhabited

blocks.note: first meaning: abandoned one's post, ran away
second meaning: empty of people, abandoned

explanation.surface: Nobody remained, so the place was left empty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of the verb for running away from duty and also an adjective for a place left empty.

clue.text: Kill-or-cure medicine?

blocks.note: surface reading: a drug that will either heal the patient or finish them off
setter's reading: any risky last-resort action taken because nothing else is left

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a description of a dangerous drug, but the phrase is used for any extreme measure taken when all else has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch measure that may succeed or make matters far worse is exactly a kill-or-cure approach.

clue.text: Mystery involved a number in regular correspondence

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so these letters are mixed up together

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A puzzling affair concerning a figure turns up in someone's routine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is the matching of parts on either side of a line, a balanced and orderly correspondence between them.

clue.text: They're the last to recognise death is near

definitions.text: They're the last to recognise death is near

blocks.clueFragment: They're the last to recognise death is near
blocks.note: surface reading: people who are slowest to accept that someone is dying
setter's reading: the final ceremonies given by a priest to a dying person, which acknowledge that the end is close

explanation.walkthrough: 'The last' looks like 'the final people', but it is part of the phrase for the sacraments given to the dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonies performed for someone about to die, called the last ones, formally mark that their end is close.

clue.text: Financial experts involved in some cost

indicators.note: involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters that follow are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Money specialists have been brought in at some expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists study money, markets and the production of wealth, so they are specialists in finance.

clue.text: They're much smarter than their mates

definitions.text: They're much smarter than their mates

blocks.clueFragment: They're much smarter than their mates
blocks.note: surface reading: people who are cleverer than their friends
setter's reading: male birds far showier than their dull-coloured female partners

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smarter' seems to mean cleverer, but here it means better dressed, and 'mates' are breeding partners, the plain peahens.
explanation.definitionFit: Male peafowl have gorgeous tail fans while the hens are drab brown, so the males are far better turned out.

clue.text: Mongrel dog sustained by meat

blocks.note: a mutt is a dog of mixed breed
to be sustained by something is to live on it

explanation.surface: A stray mongrel is kept alive on scraps of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton is the flesh of a mature sheep eaten as food.

clue.text: Fear arrest

blocks.note: first meaning: anxiety about what may happen
second meaning: the seizing of a suspect by police

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words seem to describe being afraid of being taken into custody; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both anxious dread about the future and the capture of a wanted person by the authorities.

clue.text: Declare girl in acute trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble means being in disorder, so the letters before it are thrown about

blocks.note: a girl's name
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A girl in serious difficulty makes a formal statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To annunciate is an old form of announce, meaning to proclaim or state publicly.

clue.text: Peruvian in Spain cannot be understood

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the next run of words, across a word break

blocks.note: the letters straddling the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: A Peruvian visitor to Spain finds nobody can follow what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people whose empire was centred on Cuzco in the Andes of present-day Peru.

clue.text: Wordplay of a Socratic kind

indicators.note: a kind is a sort, and sorting rearranges things, so the preceding name is reordered

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Verbal games of the sort the philosopher Socrates liked to play.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle or poem in which the initial letters of each line spell out a hidden word.

clue.text: She cleans out for the steward

indicators.note: out suggests the words are put out of their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman tidies up on behalf of the house manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was the officer in charge of a medieval noble household, managing its domestic affairs and servants.

clue.text: How mince is cooked by Chinese?

definitions.text: How mince is cooked by Chinese?

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the words before are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A question about the way Chinese cooks prepare minced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: this stir-fried noodle dish is one way minced meat appears in Chinese cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of fried noodles with shredded meat and vegetables, a way a Chinese cook serves meat.

clue.text: Free American money - and she gets a quarter

blocks.note: a buck is a US dollar
taken as written
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A woman is handed a quarter-dollar coin for nothing, in American currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarter' looks like the US 25-cent coin, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshee is British slang, originally military, for something given without charge, gratis.

clue.text: They may be eaten slowly or bolted

definitions.text: They may be eaten slowly or bolted

blocks.clueFragment: They may be eaten slowly or bolted
blocks.note: surface reading: food that can be savoured or gulped down quickly
setter's reading: fastened together with bolts, as threaded hardware pairs are

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' looks like 'gobbled down', but it also means fastened with a bolt, which these threaded fittings do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both edible kernels in shells and the small threaded fasteners screwed onto bolts.

clue.text: Light in it, for example, goes out

indicators.note: going out suggests things scattering from where they were, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A lamp is lit, but then, inevitably, it goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes out' seems to describe a light being extinguished, the opposite of the answer, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or fuse is to set it burning, to kindle it.

clue.text: Admits information is revealed in the accounts

indicators.note: something revealed within something else is found sitting inside it

blocks.note: A/C is the abbreviation for account, so accounts are ACs
knowledge is information

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that data has come to light in the company books.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge something is to concede or own up that it is true, as admitting does.

clue.text: I complain when she comes up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: taken as written
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles whenever a certain woman arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: a woman's name, the Naomi of the Book of Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, so she is someone who could be called 'she'.

clue.text: They run well, naturally, and their rise is celebrated

indicators.note: in a down entry a rise is an upward movement, so the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: something celebrated in song has been sung

explanation.surface: Fine runners, and their success is cheered by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naturally' signals these are runners in the wild: wildebeest, famous for galloping across the African plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest are antelopes that cover huge distances at speed on their annual migrations, built by nature for running.

clue.text: Bill returns with a part of her

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Bill comes back alongside a woman who has a part to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is an account; 'her' is the definition, a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Carole is a female first name, so the woman could be referred to as her.

clue.text: Involved in happy Oriental festival

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the following letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone joins cheerfully in a celebration from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the feast marks the arrival of the Magi, wise men from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Epiphany, on 6 January, is the Christian feast celebrating the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: The quality of mercy

blocks.note: surface reading: the opening of Portia's famous speech in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice
setter's reading: the characteristic trait shown by a merciful person

explanation.walkthrough: The famous quotation continues 'is not strained', but here the phrase is read literally as asking which trait mercy embodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lenient means being tolerant and forgiving, showing clemency rather than punishing harshly.

clue.text: Come into force?

blocks.note: surface reading: a law or rule taking effect
setter's reading: the armed forces, which a recruit signs up to join

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come into force' is the phrase for a law taking effect; the question mark lets the force be the army instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to become a member of one of the fighting services.
